title: Potential Gradient
notes: **Definition:** the rate of change of potential with distance: $dV/dr$.
**Relation to electric field:** $E = -dV/dr$. The electric field equals the negative potential gradient.
**Units:** V/m or N/C. Both are equivalent because $1\,\text{V/m} = 1\,\text{N/C}$.
**Physical meaning:** the potential gradient tells you how steeply potential changes in space. A steep gradient means a strong electric field.
**Graphical interpretation:** on a graph of $V$ versus $r$, the slope at any point equals $-E$ at that point. A steep negative slope means a strong field pointing inward.
